newsitem.title: USA: Declining liquor sales a factor in Ohio rating.
newsitem.headline: Declining liquor sales a factor in Ohio rating.

text.p: A decline in hard liquor consumption is a factor in the single-A rating assigned by Moody's Investors Service to a $175 million Ohio taxable Development Assistance bond issue, the rating agency reported Friday in its Credit Perspectives publication.
The bonds are backed by the state's net liquor profits.

Moody's noted that while Ohio's conversion from state-operated liquor stores to privately operated ones has saved costs and increased liquor profits, underlying trends point to declining liquor consumption.

While the bond issue is expected to ultimately win an Aaa rating based on the acquisition of insurance from AMBAC Imdenminty Corp, Moody's said it released the underlying rating "to inform investors of the credit quality of the offering absent insurance."
